## Summary

Recorded March 23, Steven Cook distinguishes tactical military damage from strategic success. He expects a messy outcome with a surviving Iranian regime, continuing containment and greater Gulf defensive spending. Eisman questions whether Trump truly seeks an exit, then reports Cook's forecast without adopting a firm regime-change prediction. June EU evidence supports continued Iranian leverage over Hormuz, but military damage, private intentions, opposition polling and uranium accessibility remain insufficiently verified.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Define strategic success separately from battlefield damage.
- Separate official policy, private interlocutors and public opinion.
- Keep nuclear enrichment distinct from an operational nuclear weapon.
- Preserve short forecast horizons even when evidence is missing.
- Assess energy sanctions licenses by their actual scope.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Strait of Hormuz navigation conditions.
- Missile-launch and production capacity.
- Gulf defense procurement.
- Iran nuclear material verification.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman hosts Steven Cook. Cook provides most regional and military analysis; Eisman's questions, disagreements and final reported takeaways remain separately identified.
- Full transcript read in two contiguous parts including closing recap.
- Explicit recording date March 23, one week before publication.
- Captions mangle Mojtaba Khamenei into ordinary words; no claims are built from that transcription artifact.
- Casualty figures and intelligence claims are attributed guest assertions, not established findings.
